Business Analytics, Master of Science (Economics and Business Administration) (2 years)

kuvaus.en: The Master's programme in Business Analytics combines business and technology in a unique way, in order to provide skills and abilities to manage and utilise digital data. The graduates will be well-equipped to confront a changing world and take on its challenges and opportunities. They will be able to use the methods and tools they have acquired in business, industrial and other organisational contexts. As business analysts they will understand data acquisition and management and demonstrate how to deploy information for business development and execution,  optimisation and decision-making.

osaamistavoitteet.en:
General Learning Outcomes:

• Analytical thinking and problem solving – our graduates are able to solve business and/or economic problems and make business decisions.

• Disciplinary knowledge – our graduates demonstrate deep and coherent understanding of an academic field of study.

• Business knowledge - our graduates demonstrate deep understanding of their own profession, and are able to use, process and analyze economic and/or business information.

• Globally responsible leadership – our graduates are able to act as future generators of sustainable value for business and society.

• Communication skills - our graduates demonstrate professional oral and written communication knowledge and skills appropriate for business situations.

After completing the Master’s Programme in Business Analytics:

Graduates are able to acquire data and organize, analyze and manipulate it for development and deployment. They know simulation and optimization means and can make use of them. They can make use of appropriate methods and tools for external (e.g. suppliers, users, customers, competitors) and internal (e.g. R&D, production, management, sales) analysis needs. Graduates know data protection, privacy and ethics principles and can work in multi-party teams and projects. They know how to develop and deploy business analytics in different environments and contexts.

After completing the degree, the student will also achieve the common generic skills of the University of Oulu, which are described on the Common generic skills and learning outcomes of the degrees page.

kuvaus.en: A scholarship is available for the second year’s tuition fee and is based on academic progress. Please visit the website of University of Oulu for further information.

The scholarship system is meant for non-EU/EEA students who are required to pay tuition fees. Please visit the website of University of Oulu for further information

teksti.en:
The programme will produce experts in analytics, who understand the needs of business, industrial and public organizations in regard to gathering, analyzing and using digital data for decision making, operations and development work. The programme addresses how to evaluate, choose and deploy the relevant analytics theories and methods and gain experience in using tools and environments for solving real-life analytics problems. The students will learn how to interpret analysis results and present them for the respective users, as well as spar and give recommendations for decision making. Simulation and optimization means are included, as well as the dynamics of actions, outcomes and contexts involved in analysis targets.

The programme addresses how to search for, gather and create research data and produce research reports based on scientific conduct in multi-disciplinary settings and different empirical contexts. In addition, responsible and sustainable business, as well as the ethics of data gathering, management and analysis principles and practices are included.  

The programme revolves around teamwork and project-based collaboration, so that problems can be solved for and with external stakeholders based also on good communication skills. The students will learn to plan and manage development projects and launch new activities involving business analytics. They will gain scientific knowledge, practical experiences and networks that will make it possible for them to continue their studies and carry out research towards a doctoral degree.

The programme involves three different degrees / main subjects in two different faculties. The Master of Science in Economics and Business Administration degree is provided by the Oulu Business School. The Master of Science in Technology degree (specializing in Computer Science and Engineering) and the Master of Science degree (specializing in Information Processing Science) are provided by the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering. The choice of specialization and thereby the degree is made when applying for the programme.

Because the programme is a multi-disciplinary entity combining data technology and information processing with business knowledge, the graduates are valued as employees by industrial and business parties and by public organizations. They can act as experts in such roles as analytics solution developers, business and data analysts, operational and strategic planning and decision-making officers and knowledge-intensive service professionals – involving also becoming entrepreneurs.

The graduates can also become entrepreneurs or be employed by analytics consultancy and development companies, in addition to working as business analytics and analytical business development professionals in companies and public organizations. They can work both as individual business analysis and development experts and act as competent members in analytics teams of SMES, public organizations and global corporations.

Because the graduates will have both scientific knowledge and hands-on skills in business analytics and there is a very high demand for analytics experts globally, they can start building international careers.

The University of Oulu Study Guide for the next academic year will be published in February. Once the Study Guide has been published, you can find the latest degree structure of the programme, including the courses required for the degree, as follows: Go to the Study Guide. Select the upcoming academic year from the academic year menu. Then select the desired level of education (for example, bachelor's programmes, master's programmes, or doctoral programmes), after which you can choose the faculty and programme you are interested in.​

Master’s thesis requirements are specific for the three respective degrees, in addition to which certain courses are required to be taken for each of the degrees.

Master's thesis is worth 30 credits. During the master's thesis work students participate in seminar sessions in which they present and report the status and advancement of their work. In the seminars they receive guidance and feedback on how to proceed in and complete their research report.

Guidelines for thesis work can be found at University of Oulu web pages.

The programme is closely connected to working life needs and opportunities. It involves close collaboration with companies and other external parties, including an extensive Capstone project in which student teams will solve problems provided by collaborating parties.

The programme is a uniquely multi-disciplinary setting with international students from various countries and with different basic degrees. The involved faculties offer several other international Master's programmes, too, so that the international degree students and exchange students from around the world provide for a versatile multicultural experiences.

The programme maintains close collaboration with leading analytics research parties around the world. The teachers of the programme are themselves active scientists in the field. The Master’s thesis required to be completed by the students is an individual research and development effort in which scientific concepts and theories are applied to solve analytics problems. In addition, many of the courses of the programme include state-of-the-art scientific publications as study materials.
The Master’s degrees earned from the programme form one of the necessary qualifications for the respective doctoral studies.

opetustapaKuvaus.en:
Different courses use different teaching and learning methods, such as independent learning, blended teaching or online teaching. In particular, first-year studies include courses with mandatory face-to-face teaching that requires students to attend sessions on campus in Oulu. Students should therefore be prepared to participate in on-campus teaching, and the programme cannot generally be completed entirely through online or independent study.

During the second year, the structure of the master’s programme provides greater flexibility, allowing students to choose courses and deepen their expertise according to their individual interests and professional goals. Teaching methods and attendance requirements nevertheless vary between courses and are specified in the individual course descriptions.

opetuskieletKuvaus.en: Finnish language studies are required for non-Finnish speaking students.

The online application at Studyinfo.fi instructs if you have to upload attachments to support your application.​

  • A proof of your English language skills. Applications without the proof of language skills will not proceed in student selection.​
  • The final diploma and academic transcript in original language. Official translations of degree certificate and transcript of records if they were issued in a language other than Finnish, Swedish, or English.​
  • A copy of passport or identity card if you are not Finnish citizen. If you are not a Finnish citizen but are exempt from paying tuition fees, please note that you must prove this by uploading a document that proves your status as a non-fee-paying applicant.​
  • Preliminary assignment​: video

More information regarding admission and language requirements on the website of University of Oulu​
